sentences.en: So when you step back and look at this big picture, Amit, groups can amplify our emotions.

sentences.en: They draw us to people with extreme views, and they especially draw us to negative emotions rather than positive emotions.

sentences.en: So generally speaking, people tend to attend to emotions in general,

sentences.en: The fact that people tend to these negative emotions mean that they're more likely to share them,

sentences.zh: 这意味着它们在人们看到的内容中所占的比例增加了。

sentences.en: We also tend to amplify emotions by aggregating that emotional information.

sentences.en: So in addition to this basic contagion effect, the fact that we overrepresent in our attention and memory stronger emotional expressions,

sentences.en: But even further, the fact that we prefer people who express more extreme emotions mean that our social networks to begin with are more emotional.

sentences.en: And so we have this cyclical loop of contagion, misperception, tie selection that contributes to that process of increased emotionality.

sentences.en: I'm wondering, Amit, if you've given thought to why our brains harness our individual emotions to the currents that run through groups.

sentences.en: I think that first and foremost, we're members of a collective system, and only after we're individuals.

sentences.en: I think that as psychologists, we're kind of trained to think of people as individual entities.

sentences.en: But really, everything that we know of individual brains is that we need social connections, just like we need water or air.

sentences.en: And our emotional experiences are not independent.

sentences.en: They're mostly collective, and they're also experienced at the individual level.
sentences.zh: 它们大多是集体的，同时也体现在个体层面。

sentences.en: And so we have very few emotions that we feel as separate individuals.

sentences.en: Many more emotions that we feel as part of family members, community members, national groups and collectives, sports fans, fan clubs, and so on and so forth.

sentences.en: And so I would urge people who think about emotions to think of emotions and emotion regulation much more in the collective than the individual level.

sentences.zh: 它始于喜悦、快乐，而在这种情况下，是热情。

sentences.en: Balmer's passion is so strong that it's contagious.
sentences.zh: 鲍尔默的热情如此强烈，以至于具有感染力。

sentences.en: He doesn't need to fake it.
And it's just a great gift that someone has as a leader.
sentences.zh: 作为领导者，这是一种伟大的天赋。

sentences.en: Rituals are also a way people can regulate collective emotions.
sentences.zh: 仪式也是人们调节集体情绪的一种方式。

sentences.en: Amit says you see rituals in religious settings, at cultural events, and on sports fields.
sentences.zh: 阿米特说，你在宗教场所、文化活动和运动场上都能看到仪式。

sentences.en: So there's all sorts of ceremonies.
sentences.zh: 所以有各种各样的仪式。

sentences.en: It starts from, you know, physical touch.
sentences.zh: 它始于，你知道，身体接触。

sentences.en: So a player is standing on the penalty line and they're fist bumping everyone in their team.
sentences.zh: 比如一名球员站在点球点上，和队里的每个人击拳。

sentences.en: I mean, why do high-intensity law firms get together and drink on Friday afternoons?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么高强度的律师事务所要在周五下午聚在一起喝酒？

sentences.en: They do this as a ritual to help resolve the anxiety that was building up during the week and get these people ready to spend some time with their family when they're not amped up from a really busy week of work.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是一种仪式，旨在帮助化解一周内积累的焦虑，让这些人准备好在忙碌了一周的工作后，能够平静地与家人共度时光，而不是处于亢奋状态。

sentences.en: Or if you think about morning rituals, for example, probably the same idea.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你想想晨间仪式，例如，可能也是同样的道理。

sentences.en: We talked about the fact that feeling negative emotions together feels better.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了这样一个事实：一起感受负面情绪会感觉好一些。

sentences.en: But it also helps us to understand that people are feeling negative emotions with us as a form both to amplify these negative emotions in a concise way, but also to control them.
sentences.zh: 但这也有助于我们理解，人们与我们一起感受负面情绪，既是一种以简洁方式放大这些负面情绪的形式，也是一种控制它们的方式。

sentences.en: And we use rituals to have a specific emotional experience in a controlled way.
sentences.zh: 我们利用仪式以受控的方式获得特定的情感体验。

sentences.en: Another way of nudging a group's emotions in a particular direction involves teaching people that their opponents are capable of change.
sentences.zh: 引导群体情绪向特定方向发展的另一种方式是教导人们，他们的对手是有能力改变的。

sentences.en: Amit, you've tested an intervention like this with a group of both Jewish and Palestinian students.
sentences.zh: 阿米特，你曾在一组犹太和巴勒斯坦学生身上测试过这样的干预措施。

sentences.en: Can you describe the intervention and tell me what happened?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下这个干预措施并告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we're in the era of hatred and hatred should be very clearly differentiated from anger.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们处于仇恨的时代，仇恨应该与愤怒有非常明确的区别。

sentences.en: When you feel angry, you want to make things right and you want to fix things.
sentences.zh: 当你感到愤怒时，你想要纠正错误，想要解决问题。

sentences.en: When you feel hatred, the person on the other side, you already established the idea that the person on the other side cannot be changed.
sentences.zh: 当你感到仇恨时，对于对方，你已经认定对方是无法改变的。

sentences.en: And there's nothing that can be done.
But you can't tell Israelis, Palestinians can change because,
sentences.zh: 但你不能告诉以色列人巴勒斯坦人可以改变，因为，

sentences.en: and you can't tell Palestinians that Israelis can change because they've been educated all their life that the other side hates them.
sentences.zh: 你也不能告诉巴勒斯坦人以色列人可以改变，因为他们一生受到的教育都是对方仇恨他们。

sentences.en: And so you have to do it in an indirect way.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须以一种间接的方式来做。

sentences.en: So we developed these leadership workshops where we talked about identifying change in general as a leader and thinking about groups as malleable entities.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们开发了这些领导力研讨会，讨论作为领导者如何识别普遍的变化，并思考群体是可塑的实体。

sentences.en: This is based on Carol Dweck's idea of malleability.
sentences.zh: 这是基于卡罗尔·德韦克的“可塑性”理念。

sentences.en: And we show that even when you teach, when you teach people about group malleability,
sentences.zh: 我们展示了，即使当你教导，当你教导人们关于群体可塑性时，

sentences.en: even when you don't tell them that they need to apply this to the specific context of the conflict,
sentences.zh: 即使你不告诉他们需要将此应用于冲突的具体背景，

sentences.en: the idea of malleability seeps into a lot of their aspects of their thinking and changes how they feel and how they think about resolving the conflict.
sentences.zh: 可塑性的理念也会渗透到他们思维的许多方面，并改变他们的感受以及他们对解决冲突的思考方式。

sentences.en: Amit Goldenberg is a psychologist at Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 阿米特·戈登伯格是哈佛商学院的一位心理学家。

sentences.en: Amit, thank you so much for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 阿米特，非常感谢你今天参加《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: There are situations where we all get to see collective emotions in action.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，我们都能看到集体情绪在发挥作用。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter if you live in a bustling city or a tiny village.
sentences.zh: 无论你住在繁华的城市还是小村庄，这都不重要。

sentences.en: It makes no difference if you're a member of a vast intergenerational household or living on your own.
sentences.zh: 无论你是庞大的多代同堂家庭的一员，还是独自生活，都没有区别。

sentences.en: You might be religious or you might be a devout atheiSt.
sentences.zh: 你可能是虔诚的信徒，也可能是坚定的无神论者。

sentences.en: Humans around the world invoke supernatural forces when it looks like their sports teams might lose.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的人们在他们的运动队看起来要输的时候，都会祈求超自然力量。

sentences.en: They take part in annual festivals that demand time, effort, and money.
sentences.zh: 他们参加需要时间、精力和金钱的年度节日。

sentences.en: They mark important moments, such as marriages, births, and deaths, with intricately choreographed scripts.
sentences.zh: 他们用精心编排的剧本标记重要的时刻，如婚礼、出生和死亡。

sentences.en: These festivals, rites, and scripts are largely designed to shape the emotions we feel collectively.
sentences.zh: 这些节日、仪式和剧本在很大程度上是为了塑造我们集体感受到的情绪。

sentences.en: The psychology of rituals perfectly complements the story we heard today from Amit Goldenberg.
sentences.zh: 仪式的心理学完美地补充了我们今天从阿米特·戈登伯格那里听到的故事。

sentences.en: Some time ago, I interviewed the anthropologist Dimitri Zigalatos.
sentences.zh: 不久前，我采访了人类学家迪米特里·齐加拉托斯。

sentences.en: He told me not only about his research, but about the time he himself was induced to take part in one of the most fearsome rituals in the world.
sentences.zh: 他不仅告诉了我他的研究，还讲述了他自己被诱导参加世界上最令人恐惧的仪式之一的经历。

sentences.en: What I also felt was this jolt of exhilaration that lasted not just for a few minutes, not just for a few hours, but in fact for several days.
sentences.zh: 我感受到的还有一种兴奋的震颤，这种感觉不仅持续了几分钟，也不仅是几个小时，实际上持续了好几天。

sentences.en: When we come back, a bonus Emotions 2.0 feature into the deep history and powerful psychology of rituals.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将带来《情绪2.0》的特别节目，深入探讨仪式的悠久历史和强大的心理学。

sentences.en: Anthropologist Dimitri Zigalatos works at the University of Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 人类学家迪米特里·齐加拉托斯在康涅狄格大学工作。

sentences.en: His research has taken him across the planet.
sentences.zh: 他的研究足迹遍布全球。

sentences.en: In his travels, Dimitri has found common cultural practices among people living in far-flung places.
sentences.zh: 在旅行中，迪米特里在遥远地区的人们中发现了共同的文化习俗。

sentences.en: Many of these practices involve dangerous, difficult, or expensive rituals.
sentences.zh: 其中许多习俗涉及危险、困难或昂贵的仪式。

sentences.en: The rituals themselves are often dramatic.
sentences.zh: 仪式本身通常是戏剧性的。

sentences.en: They are also regularly incomprehensible to outsiders.
sentences.zh: 对于局外人来说，它们也经常是不可理解的。

sentences.en: But when you peer beneath the surface, rituals actually reveal a great deal about the human mind
sentences.zh: 但当你深入表面之下，仪式实际上揭示了关于人类思维的很多信息，

sentences.en: and the psychological features that people around the world have in common.
sentences.zh: 以及世界各地人们共同拥有的心理特征。

sentences.en: Dimitri Zigalatos, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 迪米特里·齐加拉托斯，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Dimitri, some years ago, you found yourself in the Spanish village of San Pedro Manrique,
sentences.zh: 迪米特里，几年前，你发现自己身处西班牙的圣佩德罗曼里克村，

sentences.en: and you met a man named Alejandro.
sentences.zh: 你遇见了一个叫亚历杭德罗的人。

sentences.en: How did you first come into contact with him?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么第一次接触到他的？

sentences.en: So I was doing research on fire-walking rituals in Greece.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在希腊研究走火仪式。

sentences.en: That was for my doctoral research.
sentences.zh: 那是为了我的博士研究。

sentences.en: And after that, I found out that there's another place in Europe where fire-walking rituals are performed.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我发现欧洲还有另一个地方在举行走火仪式。

sentences.en: And this is this small village called San Pedro Manrique.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个叫圣佩德罗曼里克的小村庄。

sentences.en: So I just showed up there.
I started asking people if they knew about this ritual.
sentences.zh: 我开始问人们是否知道这个仪式。

sentences.en: And as it turns out, it was a really big deal in that community.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，这在那个社区是一件大事。

sentences.en: So one of the first people who others pointed me to was Alejandro.
sentences.zh: 所以别人向我推荐的第一个人就是亚历杭德罗。

sentences.en: People hold him in very high esteem in that village because he's one of the oldest fire-walkers.
sentences.zh: 在这个村子里，人们对他非常尊敬，因为他是最年长的走火者之一。

sentences.en: And he, in fact, has been doing this ritual for many decades.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他已经进行这个仪式几十年了。

sentences.en: So I understand that he was in his 70s when you were talking with him.
sentences.zh: 所以我了解到你和他交谈时他已经70多岁了。

sentences.en: Can you paint me a detailed picture of the fire-walking ritual as it was practiced in this small Spanish village?
sentences.zh: 你能为我详细描绘一下在这个西班牙小村庄里实行的走火仪式吗？

sentences.en: We are talking about a village of 600 inhabitants.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是一个只有600名居民的村庄。

sentences.en: That is in the middle of pretty much nowhere.
And yet, people have built this large open amphitheater that can host 3,000 spectators.
sentences.zh: 然而，人们建造了这个可以容纳3000名观众的大型露天圆形剧场。

sentences.en: And they only use it once a year for the purposes of this ritual.
sentences.zh: 而且他们每年只为了这个仪式使用一次。

sentences.en: So clearly, this is very important to them.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，这对他们来说非常重要。

sentences.en: On the summer solstice, every June, people start gathering in the central square.
sentences.zh: 每年六月的夏至，人们开始聚集在中心广场。

sentences.en: They engage in all kinds of processions and other celebrations throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 他们整天都在进行各种游行和其他庆祝活动。

sentences.en: And in the evening, they all join hands and they form this human chain.
sentences.zh: 到了晚上，他们手拉手形成了一道人链。

sentences.en: And they start marching up the hill in lockstep towards that venue.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始迈着整齐的步伐向山上的那个场地进发。

sentences.en: And once everybody takes their place, at exactly midnight, people start taking off their shoes.
sentences.zh: 当每个人都就位后，午夜时分，人们开始脱掉鞋子。

sentences.en: And they face a large pit of coals.
sentences.zh: 他们面对着一个巨大的煤坑。

sentences.en: This has been produced by two tons of oak wood that has been burning for hours.
sentences.zh: 这是由两吨燃烧了数小时的橡木产生的。

sentences.en: And it forms this bed of glowing coals.
sentences.zh: 它形成了一层炽热的煤床。

sentences.en: We actually measured the temperatures there at 1,200 Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 我们实际测量了那里的温度，达到了1200华氏度。

sentences.en: And while faced with this bed of coals, they take somebody on their back
sentences.zh: 当面对这层煤床时，他们会背上一个人，

sentences.en: and they walk barefoot across it on the burning fire.
And this was true of Alejandro as well.
He would carry someone across this bed of fire?
sentences.zh: 他会背着人走过这层火床吗？

sentences.en: In fact, one time I saw him carry his niece, who was significantly larger than him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有一次我看到他背着他的侄女，她比他大得多。
亚历杭德罗是个瘦小的人。

sentences.en: So he struggled to balance her on his soldiers.
sentences.zh: 所以他费力地在肩膀上保持平衡。

sentences.en: But then he just waved his hand and he went through and did it.
sentences.zh: 但他只是挥了挥手，然后走过去完成了仪式。

sentences.en: You once asked Alejandro if he would ever stop engaging in this ritual.
sentences.zh: 你曾经问过亚历杭德罗是否会停止参加这个仪式。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip of what he said in Spanish.
sentences.zh: 我想给你播放一段他用西班牙语说的片段。
伙计，总有一天会到来的。

sentences.en: Pues yo para no pasarla no tengo que subir al fuego.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果我不去参加，我就不用上火堆了。

sentences.en: Porque de la torre metilo abajo.
Can you translate what he told you, Dimitris?
sentences.zh: 迪米特里，你能翻译一下他告诉你的话吗？

sentences.en: He thought about it for a while.
And he says, well, I suppose that they will come.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，我想那一天会来的。

sentences.en: But when it does, he says, I will just not go up there.
sentences.zh: 但当它到来时，他说，我就不会再上去了。

sentences.en: And I said, what do you mean?
He says, well, I cannot go there.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，我不能去那里。

sentences.en: Because if I do that, if I saw it without being able to do it,
sentences.zh: 因为如果我那样做，如果我看着它却无法参与，

sentences.en: I would climb on the bell tower and jump off and kill myself.
sentences.zh: 我会爬上钟楼跳下去自杀。

sentences.en: So the following year, Alejandro got some news from his doctor.
sentences.zh: 所以第二年，亚历杭德罗从医生那里得到了一些消息。

sentences.en: I heard from Alejandro's son, Mamel, that his doctor told him he had detected some arrhythmia in his heart.
sentences.zh: 我从亚历杭德罗的儿子马梅尔那里听说，他的医生告诉他，检测到了心脏心律失常。

sentences.en: And therefore, he banned him from doing the ritual.
sentences.zh: 因此，医生禁止他进行这项仪式。

sentences.en: But things took a dramatic turn that night.
sentences.zh: 但那天晚上，事情发生了戏剧性的转折。

sentences.en: I was in the central square with his son, preparing for the procession that would lead us to the venue.
sentences.zh: 当时我和他儿子在中心广场，准备参加将引导我们前往会场的游行。

sentences.en: And at some point, Mamel pulled me out of the chain.
sentences.zh: 就在某个时刻，马梅尔把我从队伍里拉了出来。

sentences.en: Mamel says, come with me and you'll see.
sentences.zh: 马梅尔说，跟我来，你就知道了。

sentences.en: So he took me to his father's house.
sentences.zh: 于是他带我去了他父亲家。

sentences.en: And he announced, he said, Dad, I know you cannot do the ritual.
sentences.zh: 他宣布说，爸，我知道你没法完成这个仪式。

sentences.en: So I'm going to carry you through the fire.
sentences.zh: 所以我来背你穿过火堆。

sentences.en: And Alejandro just looked at him for a few seconds.
sentences.zh: 亚历杭德罗盯着他看了几秒钟。
然后他们抱在一起哭了。

sentences.en: And we walked towards the venue.
And indeed, Mamel was one of the first persons to walk across the fire.
sentences.zh: 确实，马梅尔是第一批走过火堆的人之一。

sentences.en: He took his father on his back.
And he crossed the burning coals.
At that point, the crowd was ecstatic.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，人群陷入了狂喜。

sentences.en: His family rushed to hike him.
sentences.zh: 他的家人冲上去想扶住他。

sentences.en: But then suddenly, Alejandro turned towards them.
sentences.zh: 但突然间，亚历杭德罗转向他们。

sentences.en: And with a sharp gesture, he told them to stop.
sentences.zh: 他做了一个尖锐的手势，示意他们停下。
所有人都瞬间安静了下来。

sentences.en: You could hear a pin drop as Alejandro turned around, facing the fire.
sentences.zh: 当亚历杭德罗转身面对火堆时，现场安静得连根针掉在地上都能听见。

sentences.en: And he just went ahead and crossed it again by himself this time.
sentences.zh: 他径直走上前，这次独自穿过了火堆。

sentences.en: You talked to Alejandro about his choice to endanger his heart against his doctor's advice.
sentences.zh: 你曾和亚历杭德罗谈过他无视医生建议、拿心脏冒险的选择。

sentences.en: What did he tell you afterwards, Demetrius?
sentences.zh: 事后他跟你说了什么，德米特里？

sentences.en: It was actually not the first time I've heard this from a firewalker.
sentences.zh: 其实这并不是我第一次从走火仪式参与者那里听到这种话。

sentences.en: My doctor said that if I do the firewalk, something terrible might happen to my heart.
sentences.zh: 我的医生说，如果我参加走火仪式，我的心脏可能会出大问题。

sentences.en: But does he know what will happen to my heart if I don't do the firewalk?
sentences.zh: 但他知道如果我不参加走火仪式，我的心脏会怎样吗？

sentences.en: You know, it seems almost that there is a theme that shows up again and again in your research into rituals.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在你对仪式的研究中，似乎有一个主题反复出现。

sentences.en: When you look at them from the outside, they can seem incomprehensible, bewildering.
sentences.zh: 当你从外部观察它们时，它们看起来可能难以理解，令人困惑。

sentences.en: But seen from the inside, the people who practice these rituals really cherish them, even when they carry significant costs.
sentences.zh: 但从内部来看，那些实践这些仪式的人确实非常珍视它们，即使它们付出了巨大的代价。

sentences.en: And in some ways, that's what you were hearing from Alejandro, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这就是你从亚历杭德罗那里听到的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, across all kinds of different contexts.
sentences.zh: 是的，在各种不同的背景下都是如此。

sentences.en: They carry so much meaning that people consider them to be a fundamental part of who they are as individuals
sentences.zh: 它们承载了如此多的意义，以至于人们认为它们是个人身份的核心组成部分，

sentences.en: and an equally fundamental part of their collective identity, who they are as group members.
sentences.zh: 也是他们集体身份——即作为群体成员身份——同样核心的组成部分。

sentences.en: So we've looked at one example of a ritual that carried enormous physical risks.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看了一个涉及巨大身体风险的仪式案例。

sentences.en: But of course, rituals also carry other forms of risks and other costs.
sentences.zh: 但当然，仪式也带有其他形式的风险和代价。

sentences.en: Tell us what pilgrims endure during the Kumbh Mela festival in India.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲朝圣者在印度大壶节期间经历了什么。

sentences.en: The Kumbh Mela is one of the most important Hindu pilgrimages in the world.
sentences.zh: 大壶节是世界上最重要的印度教朝圣活动之一。

sentences.en: And this is arguably the biggest congregation of human beings in known history.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是已知历史上最大规模的人类聚会。

sentences.en: Last time somebody counted, there were about 150 million people attending the festivities.
sentences.zh: 上次有人统计时，大约有1.5亿人参加了庆祝活动。
